sources.used_for: Section 5 requires the exact statement 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.'; Section 1 defines Special Links and the tagged-link requirement. || VERBATIM RE-READ 2026-11-20 (session 66f2548a): §5 Identifying Yourself as an Associate reads "You must clearly and prominently state the following, or any substantially similar statement previously allowed under this Agreement, on your Site or any other location where Amazon may authorize your display or other use of Program Content: 'As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases.'" §5 also bars misrepresenting or embellishing the relationship, "including by expressing or implying that we support, sponsor, or endorse you". §6 provides that "any violation of Section 5 and as specified in the Program Policies will be deemed a material breach of this Agreement", so a missing or buried disclosure is a termination-grade defect rather than a style preference - which is why the build gate fails on any page without the statement. §4 states "We do not make any representation, warranty, or covenant regarding the amount of traffic or commission income you can expect at any time"; that is the official basis for publishing no revenue forecast, conversion score or traffic estimate anywhere in this repository.

sources.title: Associates Program Policies (Commission Income Statement, Participation Requirements, IP License, Trademark Guidelines)
sources.used_for: Participation Requirements §2(a)-(b): Special Links must carry the Associates tag as a URL parameter and must be accessed directly from the site. §2(b) price clause: a site may show price and availability only if Amazon serves that data or it comes from the Creators/PA API. Also the anti-misleading-claims clause and the trademark rules. || VERBATIM RE-READ 2026-11-20 (session 66f2548a). Quoted from the page as fetched, to close the earlier excerpt caveat on §2 and to record clauses that had not been read before: · §2(a) "Special Links enable accurate tracking, reporting, and accrual of commission income. Special Links must use the Associates ID we have assigned to you." · §2(b) "you must include your Associates ID or 'tag' (appearing as XXXXX-##, or such other format as we may designate) as a parameter in the URL of each link you place on your Site to an Amazon Site." · §2(b) "You must not encourage customers to bookmark your Special Links. All Special Links must be accessed directly from your Site." · §2(b) "You must not make inaccurate, overbroad, deceptive or otherwise misleading claims about any Product". · §2(b) "You must remove from your Site any links and related references to limited time promotions as soon as that promotion on the relevant Amazon Site ends" - this puts a takedown obligation on seasonal content, not just a writing one. · §2(b) "When linking to pages with Product lists you must have additional original content on your Site that is relevant to the Special Link." · §3(b) makes the Associate responsible for disclosures "for example, if applicable, the U.S. FTC Guides Concerning the Use of Endorsement and Testimonials in Advertising", so the FTC sources are named by Amazon rather than added as a precaution. · §3(e) requires disclosing "either through a privacy policy or otherwise, the use of cookies, pixels, and other technologies by you and third parties and how you collect, use, store, and disclose data collected from visitors" (FLG-032). · §4 permits Special Links in email, SMS and direct messages only where "such communications are solicited (i.e., opted into by the receiving customer)". · §5 "You will not, without or express prior written approval, use, or allow any third party to use, any Special Links or Program Content to develop machine learning models or related technology" (FLG-030). · §6(b) "you will not create links formatted with your Associates tag for, or display such links on, a site that is not your Site." · §6(g) bars offering any consideration, reward or incentive for using Special Links, so a reader-capture offer cannot reward clicking. · §6(s) bars artificially generating clicks or impressions "whether by way of a robot or software program or otherwise", which constrains how the collector may be tested. · §6(t) "You will not display or otherwise use any of our customer reviews or star ratings, in part or in whole, on your Site unless you have obtained a link to that customer review or star rating through Creators API or PA API". · §6(u) bars purchasing through your own Special Links and bars permitting or encouraging friends, relatives, employees or contractors to do so, so gate G-02 must be tested against the tracking report rather than by placing an order. · §6(v) bars cloaking, hiding, spoofing or obscuring the URL containing Special Links including by Redirecting Links. · §6(w) "You will not use a link shortening service, button, hyperlink or other ad placement in a manner that makes it unclear that you are linking to an Amazon Site" - the clause turns on whether the destination is unclear and does not ban shorteners as such, which is why the supplied links are recorded as unresolved rather than as a violation. · §6(y) "Unless otherwise agreed by Amazon, your Site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality" (FLG-031). · Preamble: "any violation of the Associates Program Participation Requirements, the Associates Program IP License or Section 1 of the Amazon Influencer Program Policy will be deemed a material breach of the Agreement." · Commission Income Statement §1: the Session ends at the first of 24 hours elapsing, an order being placed for a non-digital Product, or a click through someone else's Special Link; cart additions count for 89 days; the item must ship and be paid for within 180 days. An untagged link never starts a Session.

sources.title: Qualify your outbound links to Google (rel="sponsored")
sources.used_for: Every outbound Amazon link on the site carries rel="sponsored". || VERBATIM RE-READ 2026-11-20: rel="sponsored" is for links "that are advertisements or paid placements (commonly called paid links)"; rel="nofollow" is for "when other values don't apply, and you'd rather Google not associate your site with, or crawl the linked page from, your site"; for regular links "you don't need to add a rel attribute". Multiple values may be space- or comma-separated, which is why the site emits rel="sponsored noopener". Such links "will generally not be followed". Page states "Last updated 2025-12-10 UTC".
sources.quote: Mark links that are advertisements or paid placements (commonly called paid links) with the sponsored value.

sources.title: 16 CFR 255.5 - Disclosure of material connections
sources.used_for: Why the disclosure sits above the fold on every page: a material connection must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously, and an affiliate commission is a material connection (Example 11).
sources.quote: When there exists a connection between the endorser and the seller of the advertised product that might materially affect the weight or credibility of the endorsement, and that connection is not reasonably expected by the audience, such connection must be disclosed clearly and conspicuously.

sources.title: 16 CFR Part 255 - Guides Concerning Use of Endorsements and Testimonials in Advertising (full part)
sources.used_for: The rule that the disclosure must be in the same place as the endorsement, not buried on a separate page.

sources.title: Google Search spam policies (including scaled content abuse and site reputation abuse)
sources.used_for: The reason this site publishes a small number of hand-checked pages rather than auto-generated pages at scale, and the reason every page has a named publisher and a contact route. Google lists affiliate links used throughout a page, with links qualified properly, among practices that are not inconsistent with its site reputation policy.
